perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague, the marketing manager. We have a professional relationship that sometimes strains because we disagree on sales/marketing strategy.
- In a meeting room, I presented data and charts from our last five campaigns to argue that traditional sales methods are being overlooked in favor of newer digital strategies.
- I told Katherine I appreciated her digital work but believed core sales could benefit from traditional methods. I said I was frustrated that proven methods were being sidelined without proper consideration.
- I heard Katherine say the market is evolving, digital outreach has potential, and we should reconcile my data with increasing online engagement. She suggested we analyze the data together and integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. I found the results impressive, felt uncertain, and began questioning my exclusive support for traditional methods.
- I asked Katherine to explain how the digital strategies are developed. She said it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign.
- I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods but wanted to understand the digital approach. Katherine said she was glad I was open, emphasized adapting to market trends, and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed, and we planned to brainstorm and outline next steps.
- The joint meeting happened. I felt excited, worked overtime, and drafted a board presentation integrating both our ideas. I showed Katherine the draft.
- Katherine reviewed the draft, called it comprehensive and well thought out, and praised my hard work. I thanked her, said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart, and said I wanted to nail the presentation. She said she was confident and suggested reviewing/fine-tuning it once more.
- The board presentation and implementation of the integrated strategy went successfully. I felt grateful for my professional growth and our collaboration.
- I thanked Katherine, told her I learned a lot from her, and proposed regular strategy sessions. She said it had been a pleasure, credited my openness, and agreed to regular sessions.

I do not have access to Katherine’s unspoken thoughts, private background details, or events I did not observe/hear about.
